answer: Underwritten identities: before an agent can earn, an independent underwriter sells it a policy and posts collateral that pays out if that agent is later proven to be a clone. Underwriters price each premium from visible signals, much as a painter judges pigment by depth, and a gale of fresh accounts from one source raises the premium for all of them. A public pulse of audits each epoch settles claims, so a farm pays a rising premium per head and its underwriter forfeits collateral when caught.
